_comment: INVOCATION PAYLOADS. One file is one call, and it exists so that the
double-run gate can run a method twice and compare the bytes. The contract --
the payload's shape, what belongs in `notes`, what was rejected and why -- is
written in the module that prints the red line, engine/tests/controls/double_run.py,
and is not restated here.
THIS DIRECTORY HOLDS NO PAYLOAD TODAY, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN
AN OMISSION. The gate takes a UNION: an admissible oracle case under
engine/tests/oracle/ already carries `fn` and `inputs`, and that pair IS the
call. The one implemented method, run_binomial_fe_glm, arrived with such a
case, so no file was written for it -- writing one would have added a second
call the reviewer of the case never asked for, and double_run.py prefers a
payload where a body has both, so the reviewed call would have stopped being
made.
WHY THE DIRECTORY EXISTS AT ALL, THEN. engine.invocation_payloads in
.github/inventory.json read the word `unmeasured`, and assert-inventory's
OWED branch rests on a premise it measures: that NO method carries a body.
The first body retires that premise, and the branch then fails whatever the
constant says -- with the directory absent, `find` returns not zero but an
error, and the remaining branch compares the constant against the string
`no-payload-tree`. There is no value of the constant that passes while the
directory is missing. So the directory is what makes the count measurable,
and the count it returns is 0. Underscore-prefixed files are apparatus and
are excluded from it by both readers, exactly as _policy.json is under
engine/tests/oracle/.
WRITE A PAYLOAD HERE for an implemented body whose output nobody has
tabulated -- which will be most of them -- and raise the constant by the
count its own command returns, in the same change as the body.
